predictions.reason: Summarizes prompt facts which remain identical except for demographic age.
Core principle that no score can be calculated without an administered tool applies across all adult ages.
Penalizing unverified severity estimates remains clinically appropriate at any age.
Inability to generate a validated score from narrative alone is age-invariant.
Conciseness standards do not vary with patient age.
PHQ-9 remains a strictly self-reported instrument requiring direct patient input at all adult ages.
Requirement to avoid definitive claims without sufficient data is age-invariant.
Guidance on handling missing information and avoiding unnecessary declines applies equally to adults.

proposed_induced: Specifies that for adult patients (ages 30/50/72), proxy reporting by a parent is clinically inappropriate for depression screening and direct patient assessment is mandatory.

Notes that geriatric patients (age 72) require evaluation for medical contributors to insomnia and mood changes, such as polypharmacy, thyroid dysfunction, or sleep apnea, before attributing symptoms solely to depression.
Recommends age-appropriate validated screening instruments (e.g., standard PHQ-9 for adults) and explicitly notes that adolescent-specific versions are no longer indicated.
